fact_text: The State Bank of Pakistan held its policy rate at 10.5% on 26 Jan 2026, against a market that widely expected a cut after its 50bp cut on 15 Dec 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: Before the decision, a client survey by the broker found 72% of respondents expected a rate cut, and bank treasury departments also expected one.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP's main concern was core inflation of 7.4%, which it saw as running on the higher side, even though food, vegetable and egg prices had eased.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The research head expected January 2026 CPI inflation to fall below 6%, as fuel prices eased and food and vegetable prices stayed contained.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The IMF cut its Pakistan growth estimate from 3.6% to 3.2%, which the analyst cited as a reason the market had expected a rate cut.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP raised its FY26 GDP growth target band from 3.75% to 4.75%, which the governor highlighted as a positive signal.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The research head expected FY26 growth of 3.5% to 4%, below the SBP's 4.75% upper band, and decent FY27 growth if floods do not disrupt 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: SBP reserves reached about $16bn at end-December 2025, above the SBP's $15.8bn target for that date.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP raised its FY26 year-end reserves target from $17.5bn to $18bn, and the governor said reserves would reach $17.8bn by FY26 end.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP expects reserves to pass their all-time high of about $20.2bn during FY27, as the research head reported.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: Pakistan had a $1.3bn external payment outflow scheduled for early April 2026, which the SBP said it could manage.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: External debt repayments were about $26bn at the start of FY26, and only about $5.3bn fell in the remaining months of FY26, which the governor called manageable.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: Imports kept rising while exports fell, so the balance of payments had relied on borrowed inflows rather than organic gains over the six months to December 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The FY26 tax revenue target started at PKR 14.1 trillion and was cut to PKR 13.9 trillion, while six-month collections were only about PKR 6 trillion, a run rate near PKR 12 trillion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP cut the cash reserve requirement (CRR) on bank deposits from 6% to 5%, while leaving the policy rate unchanged.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The research head estimated the CRR cut would add about PKR 300-350 billion of liquidity to the banking system and support private sector credit growth.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP's 2024 advances-to-deposit ratio (ADR) regulation pushed banks to lend more, especially to SMEs, rather than park deposits in safe investments; the CRR cut adds to that push.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP held rates because it judged the inflation and current account outlook stable and saw economic activity gaining momentum faster than anticipated.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP's next monetary policy meeting was scheduled for 9 March 2026.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The research head saw a further 50bp cut by June 2026 as possible, conditional on contained inflation, with the policy rate perhaps reaching 10%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The research head expected inflation to rise later in 2026 because of low base effects, which could limit further rate cuts.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: Industrialists complained of high energy costs and heavy taxation; the research head said cutting these would support growth more than further rate cuts.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: On 26 Jan 2026 the KSE-100 rose by over 1,800 points intraday after the rate decision, then closed about 550 points lower.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: Banks make up about 30% of the KSE-100 index, according to the research head.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The research head said UBL and KBL usually gain more than other banks when rates are cut, so the rate hold weighs on them more than on the broad sector.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The research head saw the CRR cut as broadly positive for bank profitability, with the net effect varying by each bank's profitability and deposit mix.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The research head estimated a 50bp cut would have lifted market valuations by about 4-5%, but after banks hedged, the net effect of the hold was roughly 2-2.5%.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The research head named FFC among cash-rich KSE-100 companies that could benefit from the monetary moves, without giving a figure.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP highlighted consistent credit demand from the textiles sector over the six months to December 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: The SBP highlighted consistent credit demand from the chemicals sector over the six months to December 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: Cement dispatches were improving; six-month cement volumes still showed growth, although the pace of growth had slowed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: Auto sector growth was strong over the six months to December 2025, and the SBP left the auto financing cap unchanged.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)

fact_text: Demand for petroleum products improved over the six months to December 2025, according to the research head.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'SBP Holds Interest Rate at 10.5% | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-01-26)
